summary.one_liner: doggo is a command-line DNS client written in Go, a modern alternative to dig that supports DoH, DoT, DoQ, DNSCrypt, TCP and UDP with concise, colored output.
summary.what_it_does: doggo performs DNS lookups from the terminal and prints results in a concise, human-readable format, with color-coded and tabular output. It also offers a JSON output mode for scripting, for example piping into jq. It supports multiple transports including DNS over HTTPS (DoH), DNS over TLS (DoT), DNS over QUIC (DoQ), plain TCP and UDP, and DNSCrypt, and it has an explicit DoH over HTTP/3 option. Other capabilities named in the README include iterative delegation tracing with --trace, reverse DNS lookups, EDNS options (Client Subnet, NSID, Cookies, Padding, Extended Errors), IDN punycode conversion, ndots and search handling, multiple resolvers with query strategies, and binding to a local source address. Defaults can be set through a TOML config file or DOGGO_* environment variables.
use_cases: look up DNS records for a domain from the terminal
query MX or other record types against a specific nameserver
make DNS queries over encrypted DoH, DoT, or DoQ
trace the DNS delegation chain for a domain
script DNS lookups with JSON output
run reverse DNS lookups for IP addresses
troubleshoot DNS resolution with debug output
notable: Supports many transports in one tool: DoH, DoT, DoQ, DNSCrypt, TCP and UDP
Iterative delegation tracing with --trace, similar to dig +trace
Config file and DOGGO_* environment variables with defined precedence
Written from scratch in Go, inspired by the Rust tool dog
Packaged for many platforms including Homebrew, Nix, Arch, Scoop and Winget
caveats: The README mentions a Globalping integration (--gp-from), which requires network access to that service
HTTP/3 must be paired with a persistent HTTPS (DoH) nameserver, per the README
Full installation and CLI reference live on an external documentation site rather than in the README
